messages:
maria: hey — trying to track down logs for request_id `0x7f3a4c9b` (came from the console trace link). Trace shows spans but I can't find the raw request lines in Logs Explorer. any quick tips?
kevin: first check the X-Request-ID header in the original request (sometimes we rewrite it at the proxy). if you have the trace link paste it, i can jump in.
observability-bot: trace: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/1955550000 — spans visible: frontend -> gateway -> inference-worker. sampling rate: 10% for frontend service (might be why logs missing).
maria: thanks — here's the trace: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/1955550000 (root span id a1b2c3). the request_id we have is `0x7f3a4c9b`.
kevin: quick checklist: 1) look for that request_id field in Logs Explorer (use `request_id:"0x7f3a4c9b"`), 2) grep gateway logs for the trace/span id, 3) if using CLI the helper is `ri logs --request-id 0x7f3a4c9b` (our CLI aliases it to `ri logs --req`).
kevin: console query example: `service:gateway request_id:"0x7f3a4c9b" | sort @timestamp desc | limit 200` — that should hit the envoy/proxy lines where we log incoming headers.
kevin: CLI one-liner: ```bash
echo 0x7f3a4c9b | xargs -I{} ri logs --request-id {} --since 30m
```
nate: note — sometimes the request ID is stored as `x_req` or `req_id` in older libs. if the console trace shows `proxy.id`/span tags instead, grep by span_id field: `rg "span_id=\"a1b2c3\""` across archived logs.
maria: tried the console query, nothing for service:frontend, but gateway returned a couple of lines with only span info, no full request body.
kevin: that usually means the worker that logs the request body didn't retain it (privacy+sampling). next, check the inference-worker logs for the trace/span id: `service:inference-worker span_id:"a1b2c3"` or `span.trace_id:"1955550000"`. also check the request metadata index — sometimes body is in `request_payload` field.
kevin: if still nothing, run this to map trace -> request_id via traces API: ```bash
curl -sS "https://api.redwood.ai/traces/1955550000" | jq -r '.spans[] | select(.span_id=="a1b2c3") | .tags[]? | select(.key=="request_id") | .value'
```
maria: ran that, it returned `null`. span tags don't have request_id.
nate: if span doesn't carry the header, then we need to correlate by timestamp + client ip: get the span start time from trace UI, then run `ri logs --since "2026-01-17T12:34:00Z" --until "2026-01-17T12:36:00Z" --service gateway | rg "client_ip" | rg "10.2.3.4"` (replace ip) — that usually narrows it.\e.g. `ri logs --service gateway --since 5m | jq -c '.[] | select(.message | contains("0x7f3a4c9b") or .message | contains("a1b2c3"))'`
maria: ok found gateway entry by timestamp, it logs `x-req-id: 0x7f3a4c9b` but the downstream inference-worker logs show `reqid=deadbeef` — looks like header rewriting at the gateway.\e
kevin: when that happens, search for the gateway->worker mapping: gateway logs should include a downstream-request-id tag (e.g., `down_req=deadbeef`). grep for `down_req=` in gateway logs near that timestamp. then use that downstream id to find worker logs: `ri logs --request-id deadbeef --service inference-worker`.
maria: did that and pulled the worker logs — found the error stack. perfect. thanks!!
nate: fyi i'll add a quick troubleshooting snippet to the docs: steps to map reqid->trace->logs (timestamp, search headers, span_id, downstream mapping).\maria: awesome. can you drop the snippet in #docs later? :thumbsup:
kevin: quick followup — i'll also add a tiny `ri` convenience flag to include `--map-downstream` that does the header mapping automatically. filing a tiny PR.
maria: great, closing this thread. :white_check_mark:
